# The first run of `npx neo-app` ends on the app, without webpack

Terminal predicate: a fresh `npx neo-app` on Engine 14 installs one dependency set once, builds only the development themes, starts a file server of the engine's own and shows the generated app, styled, without a click; and the time from Enter to that frame, measured from an empty npm cache on an ordinary machine, is stated in the release notes.

**Measured on 2026-11-20, after @tobiu asked for under ten seconds in the release** (table and reading: neomjs/create-app#80; runs [44795305477](https://github.com/neomjs/create-app/actions/runs/44795305477) and [44798720139](https://github.com/neomjs/create-app/actions/runs/44798720139)). The release candidate, the generator of `neomjs/create-app` `#78` with the engine's `dev`, takes 22.6 to 24.2 s on one hosted Linux CPU and 37.4 to 37.5 s on another, from an empty npm cache to the styled frame. With the scaffold reduced to the twelve packages a first-run step imports it takes 15.2 to 15.3 s on the slower of the two, and 8.6 to 16.8 s on an Apple M5 Max under other load (four runs). Ten seconds on the slower CPU needs more than one step:

| Step | Where it lives | What was measured |
|---|---|---|
| the scaffold installs what its first run runs | neomjs/create-app#80, built as neomjs/create-app#81 | 37.4 s to 15.3 s on the same EPYC 7763. The pull request's head reads 11.1 to 11.3 s on an EPYC 9V45 once the `postinstall` line of `neomjs/create-app` `#68` is in, and 21.3 to 21.5 s without it (run [44803313929](https://github.com/neomjs/create-app/actions/runs/44803313929)) |
| the generator's own dependencies | not filed | its fetch installs 63 packages and is 2.0 to 3.4 s of every run |
| a development theme step that imports only Node | row 3c″, Discussion 18182, 14.x | it takes eight of the twelve packages out of the first run; with a stand-in copy step, 6.9 and 7.6 s to the styled frame on the M5 Max |
| the package's own size | point 5 below, `resources/examples` | not measured for time |

`npm i --omit=dev` over one list is the npm-native route and is slower than the reduced scaffold (17.6 to 18.4 s): npm resolves the omitted packages for the lockfile.

**Measured on 2026-11-18** (`neomjs/create-app` `#71`, [comment 6968553307](https://github.com/neomjs/create-app/issues/71#issuecomment-6968553307); runs [44227540176](https://github.com/neomjs/create-app/actions/runs/44227540176), [44231048865](https://github.com/neomjs/create-app/actions/runs/44231048865) and [44233652087](https://github.com/neomjs/create-app/actions/runs/44233652087)). Three runs per arm from an empty npm cache, from the start of `npx` to the styled frame in a headless browser. Today's published generator: 86 to 87 s and 131 to 133 s on two hosted Linux runners with different CPUs, 288 to 289 s on a link shaped to 10 Mbit/s and 100 ms, 816 to 879 s on hosted Windows runners (two jobs). The 14.0 path as it stands on the generator's `main`: 30 to 32 s on a hosted Linux runner, 180 to 189 s on the shaped link and 570 to 615 s on a hosted Windows runner; the install is 23 s, 148 s and 498 s of that. Five seconds is met in no arm. Not measured yet: the path with the file server.

## Problem scope

The first run is the first impression the engine makes, on a person and on a coding agent alike. Measured on 2026-11-17 (`neo-app@13.4.1`, `neo.mjs@13.4.0`, Apple M5 Max, one run per condition): 64.4 s from an empty npm cache, 41.0 s with a warm one.

| Phase | Cold |
|---|---:|
| highlight.js step of `build-all`: an unpinned `git clone`, `npm install` of 447 packages, upstream's build script | 23.9 s |
| webpack, `dist/development` and `dist/production` | 11.3 s |
| workspace `npm i`, 520 packages | 9.8 s |
| `npx` fetching the generator, which lists the engine as a dependency it never imports | 6.6 s |
| a second `npm i` inside `node_modules/neo.mjs`, 525 packages | 6.2 s |
| `dist/esm` and the path check | 3.5 s |
| themes | 1.7 s |

What the run needs is far less. Dev mode reads one thing a build produces, the development themes (1.0 s). A full `build-all` passes without the nested install, which adds 491 MB. The engine as the only dependency installs in 1.7 s from an empty cache, and the generated app renders 0.2 s after navigation. And the run does not end on the app at all: `server-start` is `webpack serve --open`, which opens a directory listing of the workspace root, two clicks away from the app.

The dev server is also the heaviest tree in the lockfile. Of the engine's 560 lockfile entries, `webpack-dev-server` alone keeps 155 installed and webpack's four packages 211. Its config has no entry: it starts webpack to serve files.

**Why an Epic.** The outcome spans two repositories (the engine and the generator), its leaves break two live consumers at the merge and so land paired, and it is one measurable result: the run from Enter to the visible app.

## Intended solution shape

Selected in https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/21210 (Axes 1 and 2). @tobiu's input governs the cut: 14.0 is the window for breaking changes, and a clean cut with an upgrade note is preferred to a migration path. Compatibility binds within a major only.

1. **The generator builds what dev mode reads.** After the install it runs the development theme build and names `npm run build-all` for the three dist environments. Filed as neomjs/create-app#69.
2. **One install.** The generated `postinstall` loses its nested `npm i`; the scaffold declares the packages a postinstall or scaffold step imports, and the parity check asserts that (neomjs/create-app#68). The generator loses its own engine dependency (neomjs/create-app#61). Amended on 2026-11-20 by the epic's owner: the scaffold declares only the packages a first-run step imports, and the build tools arrive with the first build (neomjs/create-app#80, which reopens row 2b of the Discussion and answers its falsifiers).
3. **The highlight.js bundle is built from the installed package** with esbuild (#21211). Under point 1 it leaves the first run; it stays in `build-all` and CI.
4. **A file server of the engine's own replaces `webpack serve`.** One engine leaf and one generator leaf.
   - The command line is chosen once and its callers move together: `npm run server-start -- --port <n> --no-open` keeps working for the six Playwright configs that start it, and `PORT` keeps selecting the port for the agent seats' launcher.
   - It serves the working directory with `.mjs` and `.wasm` MIME types and range requests, serves the engine's release-notes directory while every other dot-directory stays closed, and carries today's development-theme freshness warning.
   - With `--open` in a workspace it opens the app the generator wrote, not the root listing. That closes the directory-listing finding; the generator leaf owns it (`neomjs/create-app` `#72`).
   - The generator copies the docs app only on request. Row 1d selected `copyDocsApp` as opt-in, so the default first run copies nothing (`neomjs/create-app` `#72`).
   - `buildScripts/webpack/webpack.server.config.mjs` is deleted, not kept as a deprecated entry, and `webpack-dev-server` leaves the engine's and the generated dependency lists.
   - Named by the old path inside the engine: `.claude/launch.json`, `.github/workflows/classify-test-scope.yml`, two unit specs and a fixture, `buildScripts/create/component.mjs`, `buildScripts/README.md`, `learn/agentos/RunningTheFleetCockpit.md`, `learn/benefits/body/FourEnvironments.md`.
   - One consumer breaks at the merge, not at the release, and lands in the same hour: a private package repository, whose `server-start` runs the engine's webpack binary with that path. Until 2026-11-18 this point also named the Institution. It runs a `webpack.server.config.mjs` of its own with its own `webpack-dev-server` and is not reached (the steward's read, comment 6967621246; confirmed at its e8477f6f). devindex, Stage and pages move when they bump the engine. Thirteen other public repositories that name the path are pinned to engine 4 to 9 and are not reached.
5. **The package ships less, first step.** The engine's own `*.spec.mjs` files (13.9 MB in 1,066 files) and `apps/portal` (9.1 MB) leave the npm package, after a fresh workspace has shown that `test-unit`, `build-all` and `server-start` work with the Playwright configs and fixtures alone. `resources/examples` (13.9 MB) stays until `copy-examples`, which reads it, is decided. Split on 2026-11-18: see the paragraph below the steward's.
6. **The bar and how it is measured.** From Enter on `npx neo-app` with the defaults accepted to the styled app visible on its own, the server start and the icon requests included, from an empty npm cache. Measured on two machines, one of them ordinary, and once under a slow network, with the conditions of every run reported (`neomjs/create-app` `#71`). Five seconds is the operator's target; today's single-machine numbers do not certify it.

**Gate for 14.0** (the steward of the cut, comment 19669790): the engine leaf, the generator leaf and the paired consumer changes are merged with the e2e suites green by Fri Nov 20, so the release reading runs them. If that fails, the row moves, and the next window is the operator's to name.

**Moved on 2026-11-17, 17:28Z, by the steward** (her fork B, after that day's holder call). The pair and its two consumer changes are four pull requests that each need a reviewer of another family before Friday night, and review by another family was the scarce thing that week; the server would also change under all six Playwright tiers three days before the release reading. So point 4 splits:
- **In 14.0:** a generator-only leaf, which @neo-opus-vega files: the docs copy as opt-in and the open target on today's server, so the first run ends on the app.
- **In the first 14.x minor, as an additive change** (the steward's decision, comment 6955736494, which replaces the clause above about the operator naming the window): #21215 and `neomjs/create-app` `#72`. The file server lands beside today's config. `buildScripts/webpack/webpack.server.config.mjs` stays in the package for workspaces created before it, so no consumer breaks at the merge and the paired landing falls away; its deletion and the upgrade note wait for the next major. Where point 4 above says deleted, this staging governs.

**Restored on 2026-11-18 by the steward** (comment 6967621246, which replaces the staging above). Her first reason fell away: the Gemini window reset early, so two more seats can review. Point 4 is back in 14.0 as the clean cut, under the gate of comment 19669790 with three pull requests instead of four: #21215, `neomjs/create-app` `#72` and the private package's `server-start`, merged with the e2e suites green by Fri Nov 20. If they are not, the staging of 2026-11-17 stands. If a tier turns red on a server cause after the merge and before the lock, the three are reverted, not repaired forward, and that staging stands as well. @neo-opus-vega holds all three. @neo-opus-ada's read (#21215, comment 6967673674) added a `Host` check, a MIME criterion and a timing guard to #21215. HTTP/3 stays out of 14.0: Node keeps `node:quic` behind an experimental flag, and the engine's floor is Node 24. What a multiplexed transport is worth to `dist/esm` is measured in #21216, pulled forward on the same day.

**Point 5 split on 2026-11-18 by the epic's owner**, after its consumers were read at `dev` `bdfc6a71ce` (numbers and receipts: #21313).
- **The spec files leave in 14.0** (#21313): 1,111 files, 13.69 MiB unpacked, 3.04 MiB compressed. The precondition as worded above cannot be met. The generator's four test commands run the engine's Playwright configs, whose `testDir` is the engine's own tree, so they run the engine's suite and exit 1 once the spec files are gone. The generator stops writing them in the same release (neomjs/create-app#76, where the three rows of this fork are recorded). That answers the `STEP_BACK`'s "each test command a workspace is still promised": a 14.0 workspace is promised none. One that tests its app owns a Playwright config and imports `test/playwright/setup.mjs` or `fixtures.mjs`, which stay in the package.
- **`apps/portal` does not leave in 14.0.** The deployed site is built from the Portal inside the installed package (`neomjs/pages`, `buildScripts/updateNeoVersion.mjs`; the SSR middleware links that copy), and the consumer build check compiles it as its specimen. The order for a later release: the site takes the Portal from the release tag, one deploy proves it, then the package drops it (1,295 files, 6.47 MiB unpacked, 2.94 MiB compressed). Not filed.
- **`resources/examples` is the byte lever:** 12.42 MiB of the 23.61 MiB tarball. Unchanged, it waits for `copy-examples`.
- **What the trim is worth to the first run.** The package is 6,646 files; the engine's clone holds 31,047 more in `node_modules` for its 560 lockfile entries, a proxy for a workspace's dependency tree. The spec files are about 3 % of what an install writes. This step is package hygiene; the bar of point 6 moves with the dependency trees of point 4.

The steward of the cut may set another line for either half.

**Carried from the `STEP_BACK`** (comment 19669743). Each partial is owned by a leaf:
- Consumers: the server leaf updates its callers together and keeps no deprecated webpack entry. The first run, the docs and example copies, and each test command a workspace is still promised get a witness of their own. Windows is unmeasured.
- Density and UX: the measurement of point 6 is `neomjs/create-app` `#71`, and the release notes take its number.
- Existing primitives: `developmentThemeAssets.mjs` checks the freshness of SCSS output; the server leaf carries the warning without assuming it certifies anything else.
- Authority: `Decision Record: OPTIONAL`. The server's command line and what it serves are recorded in its leaf and in `buildScripts/README.md`.

## Out of scope

- **Plain CSS in place of SCSS** (Axis 3): Discussion 18182. Its breaking half targets 14.0 under its own gate.
- **What builds or replaces the bundled environments** (Axis 4): measured on 2026-11-18 (#21216); the choice is Discussion 21311, aimed at 14.1.
- **Two packages, runtime and toolchain** (row 2c): deferred to the planning after 14.0.
- **Trimming `resources/examples`** from the package: waits for a decision on `copy-examples`.

## Avoided traps

- **Keeping the old config path as a deprecated entry.** Rejected with the clean cut: the consumers that matter are few and named.
- **A dev-only dependency list** (row 2b). npm has no lazy dependency group, and a second list is a second thing to keep in step; removing trees reaches the same goal.
- **Loading the engine from a CDN** (row 2d). Every worker needs a same-origin shim, and the CDN copy carries no CSS.
- **Shipping built CSS in the package** (row 3b). It changes the rule that the package carries no generated output, for the engine's sheets only.
- **Building nothing and letting the server build on demand** (row 1c). The theme hook only warns today.
